verses: The nine inclosures of the net The rud and bream keep tight. Our prince in dragon robe we see, And skirt with figures bright.
The geese brief time fly round the isles; Home bends the duke his way. 'Twas only for two passing nights He deigned with us to stay.
Back to the land now fly the geese; The duke comes not again. 'Twas only for two passing nights He could with us remain.
Short time the single dragon robe Among us we have had. Our duke, O take not to the west, Nor bid our hearts be sad!
